items.guidance: Read standalone/entrypoint.sh to find the server it starts (for example gunicorn or uwsgi) and the bind address and port it passes; the facts give port 8000. Declare that port with EXPOSE in standalone/Dockerfile, and add ENV PORT only if the entrypoint or the Django settings read PORT.

Check the project urls.py files for an existing status or ping URL before adding one. If you add one, a small view that returns an HttpResponse with status 200, included in the standalone project's root urls.py, is enough. If SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, APPEND_SLASH, or ALLOWED_HOSTS would block the probe, answer the path from a small middleware placed first in MIDDLEWARE instead of relaxing those settings.

Check the settings for MEDIA_ROOT and other paths under /data, and classify ticket attachments and uploads as persistent while collected static files can stay in the image. If django-storages is already installed, configure its S3 backend through STORAGES or DEFAULT_FILE_STORAGE with the bucket name read from STORAGE_BUCKET and no access keys. Keep the FileSystemStorage default when the bucket variable is not set.

Search for the Celery app module (for example a celery.py next to the settings), task definitions, and any beat schedule, and check entrypoint.sh and standalone/docker-compose.yml for a celery worker or beat command. Report the exact production command if one exists, whether beat is used, and which broker URL setting Celery reads, because the facts list no broker that Deployz provides.
